macro.headline: Bull regime intact but momentum cracking — VIX spike + bearish MACD vs. price above SMAs.
macro.story:
The tape is sending a mixed message. SPY and QQQ are still above both their 50- and 200-day moving averages, the Russell 2000 is making fresh momentum highs (RSI 63), and the Dow is leading with bullish MACD — the bull regime is structurally intact, with SPY only ~1.7% off its 52-week high. But under the surface, momentum has rolled over: SPY's MACD is now below its signal line with a negative histogram, the index sits below its mid-Bollinger band, and VIX has jumped +21% in five days to 19.6 while still holding above its 50- and 200-day averages. Price is above the trendlines; momentum and volatility are not confirming. That's the textbook setup for treating this as a transitional zone rather than a clean continuation.

The dominant cross-asset driver, grounded in the active themes, is the AI Infrastructure capex cycle (CHASING stage, conviction 8). Capital is concentrating into the AI compute stack while precious metals get unwound as funding — gold -4.5% in 5 days, silver -11.8%, both now below their 50- and 200-day averages with RSIs in the low 30s. The dollar (DXY) is overbought-extended at RSI 74.5 and up 1.7% in five days, which is the validated headwind keeping pressure on gold and silver. WTI crude has collapsed -23.8% over 21 days (RSI 28.5) — the Iran-deal / Hormuz-reopening theme in the data describes exactly this geopolitical risk-premium unwind, and it's a tailwind for consumer-facing and travel names but a body blow to energy producers.

The yield-curve story matters here too. The 10Y–2Y spread has compressed -51% over 21 days to just 0.26, with the 2Y up and the 10Y drifting lower — a flattening that signals the market is pricing more growth caution even as equity indices hold up. Combined with the VIX spike, this is the bond market hedging what the equity tape has not yet priced.

For a long-only book: the validated Early-Runway rotation tailwind is active in several industries (more in the industries section), and the bull regime gives those signals room to work. But macro confidence is LOW because the indicator alignment is genuinely broken — price above SMAs, MACD bearish, VIX spiking, commodities collapsing, curve flattening. Hunt selectively in confirmed rotation winners; do not assume the broader tape will bail out marginal setups.

active.name: AI Infrastructure Build-Out — Mega-Cap Compute & Software
active.thesis: Institutional capital is concentrating into the AI compute stack — silicon (NVDA, INTC), infrastructure software (MSFT, PLTR), and the platform/ad layer monetizing inference (META, AAPL). With VIX at 15.88, bullish put/call, and SPY above 50SMA, the TRANSITIONAL regime is being expressed through quality mega-cap tech rather than broad risk-on, suggesting capital is rotating UP the quality curve rather than out.
active.evidence: XLK accel_ratio 1.715 and QQQ accel_ratio 3.323 (14d bull rate 3.3x the 60d baseline) show genuine fresh acceleration, not just persistence. Software-Infrastructure (1.992) and Consumer Electronics (2.246) are leading the doubling-up.

active.name: Natural Gas Reversal — Early Commodity Flip
active.thesis: Natural gas has flipped from ACCELERATING_BEARISH to bullish (+0.37%/day 14d) while crude oil and broader energy commodities (USO, BNO, DBC) are flipping the other way — a divergence that historically signals supply-side gas tightening (storage draw, weather, or LNG export demand) independent of macro oil weakness. Early-stage and contrarian to the broader commodity tape.
active.evidence: UNG is the ONLY commodity in the universe with a bearish-to-bullish flip; every other energy and ag commodity is rolling over. The asymmetry is the signal — but 60d base is still -9.96%, so this is an inflection trade, not a confirmed trend.

invalidators.condition: UNG trajectory returns to DIRECTION_FLIP_bullish_to_bearish or ACCELERATING_BEARISH
EIA weekly storage report prints materially above estimates (bearish surprise)
14d rate decelerates below +0.15%/day for 5 consecutive sessions

active.name: Geopolitical Risk Unwind — Iran Deal / Hormuz Reopening
active.thesis: The Iran nuclear deal and the Strait of Hormuz reopening have resolved near-term crude supply-disruption risk. WTI crude has fallen approximately 5% to near $80/barrel as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds. This is unambiguously RISK-ON for equities: lower crude reduces input-cost and inflation-expectation pressure, eases the case for further Fed tightening, and removes the dominant macro tail-risk from the narrative. The correct read on oil weakness here is NOT 'Iran re-escalation risk' — it is the OPPOSITE: the Hormuz corridor is reopening and supply constraints are lifting. Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.
active.evidence: WTI crude ~$80 (-~5% from recent highs); crude trajectory shifting from HOLDING_BULLISH toward FADING_BULLISH/bearish. Natural gas divergence intact (independent supply story — not demand-driven). Broad commodity complex already fading (DBC, USO, BNO).

invalidators.condition: Iran deal collapses or Hormuz incidents resume — crude reverses sharply higher
OPEC+ emergency production cut to defend $80 floor offsets supply increase

newsletter:
**[THE SPINE]** Dollar strength is the dominant force this week, and it is silently rewriting the cross-asset map. DXY at 101.29 is sitting above its upper Bollinger band with RSI 74.3 and a +2.1% 21-day push, and the ACTIVE DXY_METALS_TAG signal (backtested HOLDS, -0.45 sustained correlation) is doing exactly what it advertises: Gold -8.9% on 21d, Silver -18.6%, Copper -1.4%, Oil -23.7%. The precious metals and broad commodity themes are explicitly fading on the dashboard. Everything below hangs off this dollar regime.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop is CHOPPY/TRANSITIONAL (confidence 6/10) but the dollar spine is unambiguous. VIX 19.97 with a 21% three-week pop and 17% one-day spike tells you hedging demand is rebuilding even as SPY holds +2.1% over its 50SMA — that is a fragile equilibrium, not a green light. Yields are NOT mean-reverting: the 2Y is overbought (RSI 78.7, above upper band) and the 10Y ceiling signal explicitly DOESN'T HOLD per backtest, so treat 4.49% on the 10Y as trend, not resistance. Oil at RSI 28.6 is a trend, not a bounce setup — the WTI oversold edge is negative (-3.87%, 51% hit). The signal that matters is the active DXY headwind on hard assets; respect it.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Under the dollar regime, rotation is flowing into domestic cyclicals and tech, away from anything commodity-linked. XLK +8.6%/21d is ACCELERATING_BULLISH, IWM +6.8% and XLI +6.8% are tagged leaders, XLF +4.3% and XLB +4.2% round out the leadership. Industry-level flow is concentrated into Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and the AI Infrastructure theme (stage=CHASING, day 22, health 8.0). Precious metals and broad commodities are explicitly in the FADING bucket — do not try to catch them while DXY is above its 21/50d.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The clearest "already run" warning is Semiconductors: 13 months hot, +258% gain — that is the record, with a CEILING flag. Same story in Semi Equipment & Materials: 12 months, +288%, CEILING. These are exit-management names, not entries. The in-range setups with smart-money flow are in Specialty Industrial Machinery — AME (coil 72%, bullish flow) and GEV (coil 97%, bullish flow) — and PGR in P&C insurance (coil 83%, bullish flow). Software - Infrastructure is still early in its heat spell (1 of typical 7 months, only +3% in) and is ACCELERATING_BULLISH at the trajectory level — that is the asymmetric side of the AI spine versus the extended semis.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is DXY. A break back below the 21d/50d cluster (roughly 99.4 support) invalidates the active DXY_METALS_TAG and would reopen Gold/Silver/Copper as buyable rather than fading. Conversely, DXY pressing higher with VIX following through above 21.6 resistance means the choppy regime tips bearish and the AI/cyclical leadership gets tested. Also remember: any bounce in Gold or Oil from here is a washout candidate — 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days, so do not call a bottom on one green print.
